anya: ran an nsys trace on the canary that hit the slow path, uploading timeline: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1782101120 :eyes:

mike: saw it — big queue tail after ~1200 tokens into long prompts, queue-time jumps from ~9ms to ~28ms for some requests

sam: what changed in runtime? batcher tuning? kernel swap?

anya: we switched kernel selector for attn to pick `attn_fwd_tiled_qk` for sequence lengths >512 to reduce memory pressure, but perf looks worse for mixed lengths due to fragmentation. also added a kvcache sweep that runs on evict which may be serializing requests

devon: metric dump from the run: `prefix_kvcache_hit_rate=0.74, avg_queue_ms=20.9, p99_lat_ms=142, compute_ms=5.8` — baseline before change: `hit_rate=0.98, avg_queue_ms=8.9, p99=88`

mike: whoa hit_rate drop from 98% -> 74% explains more fetches and queuing. why did hits drop?

anya: trace shows kvcache key normalization off-by-one for patched segment ids; keys for some prefixes got canonicalized differently, causing misses. look for NVTX range `[KVCACHE::lookup]` spikes in the timeline.

perf-bot: nsys summary: top kernels by total time: `attn_fwd_tiled_qk` 45%, `softmax_block` 18%, `kv_read_batch` 12%, memcpys 9%

sam: is `attn_fwd_tiled_qk` slower than old fused kernel per token or just higher because of more calls?

anya: per-call time is slightly lower but call count increases due to shorter dispatch windows (batcher started splitting cross-length batches into more micro-batches). throughput lost because we pay launch overhead more often. timeline shows many tiny kernels back-to-back with small gaps (~20-50us) but those gaps add up into queueing at scale.

devon: batcher config in canary: `max_window_ms=8, min_window_ms=1, frag_threshold=0.25` — we lowered window to reduce tail latency but kernel selector plus kvcache misses created feedback loop: more misses -> longer lookups -> more queue -> smaller observed batching windows -> more micro-dispatches

mike: change suggestion: revert kernel selector for mixed-length profile and fix kvcache normalization. also consider coalescing tiny launches in the runtime when gap < 100us

anya: tried a quick experiment: patched normalization + bump `max_window_ms=16` on canary. new trace shows `hit_rate=0.96, avg_queue_ms=10.6, p99=95, compute_ms=6.0` — much closer to baseline. timeline: fewer `kv_read_batch` NVTX ranges and larger contiguous kernel blocks.

sam: nice. can you paste the nsys CLI you ran so we can reproduce?

anya: sure: ```bash
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_1782101120 --trace=cuda,osrt,exp --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --target-processes=all --export=sqlite ./canary_runner --profile-config=config/canary.yaml
```

devon: also capture perfetto (system-wide) for next run to see CPU jitter — I saw some host threads blocking on `kvcache::sweep_lock` in perf events

mike: follow-up tasks: 1) revert kernel selector condition for mixed-lengthes (sam), 2) fix kvcache key normalization (devon), 3) add tiny-launch coalescer in dispatcher (anya), 4) run nsys+perfetto end-to-end and validate p99 (everyone)

anya: going to post the trimmed perf timeline and a short guide to interpret NVTX markers under /internal/docs/trace-playbook.md :book:

sam: thanks — logging task tickets now and will run a non-canary repro on dedicated infra later today

perf-bot: deploybot: canary build 2026.03.30-197 reverted kernel-selector flag (sha: a1b2c3f), new canary trace scheduled at 1782107200

mike: great thread. short-term fix looks solid. we should also add a regression test that asserts kvcache hit_rate > 95% on standard prompt corpus to catch this earlier.

anya: agreed. I'll add an integration eval that runs a mini-workload and checks hit rates + queue ms thresholds.

devon: FYI I dug into the normalization patch — PR up now: https://git.redwood/p/r/3421 — please review

sam: review incoming :eyes:

anya: thanks all, will follow up with results after scheduled run
